entry.title: Matematik Alpöge s pomocí SI možná rozlouskl Riemanna

Svůj důkaz uvolnil jako open-source kód o 17 milionech řádků jazyka Lean, pro formální verifikátor teorémů Lean 4, dohromady ve čtrnácti *.tar.gz archivech (https://alpo.ge/lean.tar.gz.part01 až https://alpo.ge/lean.tar.gz.part14).Světové vědecké kapacity i amatérští nadšenci nyní horečně kompilují a analyzují tento čerstvý matematický důkaz, ačkoliv se zdá být validním, přesto se objevují i pochyby. Leven Alpöge se podílel také na předchozí matematické bombě, důkazu Navier-Stokese.

entry.title: USN-9183-1: Linux kernel (FIPS) vulnerabilities
Patentový terror Synapticsu zabil ovladač Vino
entry.summary: Skotský vývojář Mike Lothian pozastavil vývoj svého otevřeného ovladače Vino (nedostupné) pro dokovací stanice DisplayLink poté, co mu Synaptics v reakci na žádost o pomoc pohrozil žalobou kvůli údajnému porušování patentů. Firma nejprve předložila seznam 125 patentů bez specifikace, které konkrétně měl ovladač porušovat, a následně požadovala 25 tisíc dolarů za náklady na jejich přiřazení ke kódu s hrozbou, že se tato částka bude každým týdnem o stejnou sumu navyšovat. Dále tvrdila, že DisplayLink není členem Open Invention Network, ačkoli jeho mateřská společnost Synaptics jejím členem je. Otevřený ovladač označila za hrozbu pro svou konkurenční výhodu, protože by prý odhalil fungování jejích proprietárních technologií. Synaptics po právních výhrůžkách dokonce reagoval na Lothianův dlouhou dobu ignorovaný pull request do projektu EVDI a požádal ho o další úpravy, Lothian je odmítl provést s tím, že mu firma nemůže nejdřív hrozit žalobou a pak žádat o nějakou další spolupráci.

entry.summary:
Pražský MobileLinux Hackday je zpět, tentokrát už s devátým pokračováním! Už tento pátek 20. listopadu od 10:00 se opět sejdeme v Praze v SUSE. Přijďte si popovídat o Linuxu na telefonech, poslechnout si pár krátkých přednášek a hlavně si společně něco rozběhat, opravit nebo naprogramovat.
Na programu máme přednášky o tom, proč potřebujeme „nudné“ telefony s Linuxem (spoiler: platby), co dělat s vlastním open source projektem, když už jste ho naprogramovali, nebo o NixOS a JTAG.
A hlavně budeme hackovat! Přineste si vlastní telefon a pomůžeme vám na něm rozběhat Linux. Budeme mít i hromádku starších telefonů, které si můžete sami flashnout a klidně si je odnést domů na další hraní.
Chceme také rozběhat češtinu ve Stevia klávesnici, ideálně s grafickou akcelerací, pořádně otestovat OpenVlak (otevřenou alternativu k aplikaci ČD Vlak) a samozřejmě se dostane i na aplikace, služby, linuxové jádro, LLM/AI a cokoliv dalšího, co si přinesete.
Nemusíte být vývojáři ani mít zkušenosti s mobilním Linuxem. Stačí zvědavost a chuť si něco vyzkoušet.
Registrace je nově možná na tuxies.cz/registrace.
Pro další informace a diskusi se připojte k naší komunitě Mobilní Linux Československo na Matrixu. Novinky najdete také na Mastodonu.

entry.title: Remembering the back alley brawls of The Warriors, a Rockstar city game that isn't an open world
entry.summary: The older I get, the more fascinated I somehow become by how videogames depict night, how particular technologies at particular times give rise to particular nightlives. I've already gushed about the Starlight Zone in Sonic the Hedgehog – the mild dissociation incubated by the soft, ceaseless glare of the construction yard, the eyeless brick at the level's nadir, the sleepless glitter of the skyline. Now, let me wind the clock forward, and backward, to Rockstar Toronto's The Warriors. One long night from the late '70s, sweaty and electric and menacing, fed through dank and sullen polygons from 2005. Probably the best move Rockstar made with their adaptation of Walter Hill's film is to retain the element of phantasmagoria. Both the game and the movie open with a view of Coney Island's Wonder Wheel, its neon lamps forming a floating tracery of Morse code, cabins swinging almost imperceptibly against solid darkness. I realised, however, in 2019 that I was a kind of sleeper agent: whenever I heard the opening notes of Legends of Azeroth, the original World of Warcraft login screen music, I would feel the reactivation of a latent part of my mind laid down when I was 10 years old. And so, like a form of possession, whenever Blizzard announces a new legacy iteration of the original WoW, no downpayment in time nor money is too great to prevent me from returning. Here I am, then, at the launch of World of Warcraft: Forever, seven years after Blizzard first revived the original 2004 game with World of Warcraft Classic in 2019. Once more I set foot on Durotar, to spend as much time as I can levelling up a new Orc Warrior before I am forcibly unplugged by either my boss or, more likely, my wife, and so far it's been a welcome return to some of the frictional - but more involving and consequential - socialising that WoW's decades of updates had previously sanded down. entry.summary: At this point the tragedy of Driv3r, or Driver 3, or my personal favourite Drive-thrur, is well thumbed. A familiar litany of unrealised ambition, heinous bugs, dull open-world design, and an expensive yet audibly bored voice cast, the accidental comedic highlight of which is Michelle Rodriguez flatly reeling off car theft orders from what sounds like the inside of a Michelle Rodriguez-sized tupperware container. A more widely forgotten detail is that, for a while, there was a non-zero chance - a belief, even - that Drive Three Er was going to be the opposite. The 2003-2004 hype cycle had sowed the notion that this would in fact be the open-world crime thriller to knock Grand Theft Auto off its perch, and even 22 years before GTA 6's idolising reviews, that was no small promise; Rockstar were still enjoying the balmy success of Vice City, and we could see San Andreas cresting the hill on a stolen, shining BMX. "Ah, but did they have Michael Madsen doing doughnuts in car parks?," publishers Atari asked the world, either unaware or in denial of the spluttering, clapped-out rattletrap they were about to wheel into the showroom. You likely know the rest, though one of the dangers of familiarity is the subsequent breeding of complacency, which in this case can manifest as a thawing acceptance. I succumbed to this myself, having recently installed a legally unlinkable copy of Drivethreeuh, mind opened to the possibility that maybe it wasn't that bad. How Origame Digital are channelling and defacing Lovecraft over a trilogy of "inherently indigenous" anti-fascist games
entry.summary:
Much like the H.P. Lovecraft novella it alternately riffs on and skewers, Penguin Colony takes you to an ancient alien city of crabby cuboid geometry and helical designs – comparable at a glance to Lovecraft's "terraces of every sort of provocative disproportion", but here given strangely everyday, anachronistic-seeming labels, such as "Downtown". Later, you're shown flashes of footage of the streets of Melbourne in Australia - developer Origame Digital's base of operations, and a city built on stolen Wurundjeri Woi-wurrung and Bunurong Boon Wurrung land.
When I first set foot in Downtown, in the unassuming body of a Rockhopper penguin, I thought the broad idea was to satirically redefine modern settlements built by European colonisers as Lovecraftian relics, intrusions from the cosmic beyond. This irony seems most pointed in sections where you steer a group of Māori characters, journeying south to prevent an expedition of German and British Nazi occultists from resurrecting a surviving elder being they call the "one true Aryan king". Playing as one of the Māori voyagers, you witness the cyclopean city as a realm of spectral high rises and square windows, rearing out of a swamp of blood and bone.

entry.title: "A fight for all workers": SAG-AFTRA throw weight behind emerging Rockstar union ahead of its GTA 6 release week vote
entry.summary: In what has come to feel like the dawn of the final day before Grand Theft Auto VI's release, one thing that Rockstar really don't want people to be aware of is the ongoing legal dispute between the Rockstar Games Workers Union and the studio itself following Rockstar's alleged union busting in firing 31 union members last year. Starting on the 12th through to the 26th, recognition of the union will be voted upon by staff to ensure that workers would be given a say over "topics including pay and bonuses, overtime, redundancies, flexible working arrangements, and generative AI policies." If it passes, the vote would also make the union the largest recognised union in the UK games industry, partly thanks to its partnership with the Independent Workers Union of Great Britain. Now, the global labor union SAG-AFTRA have chimed in to endorse the Workers Union, offering solidarity to the members involved and granting important leverage from a global force. Read more
